slices.label: Byzantium's darkest hour
events: Persia holds Jerusalem, Antioch and Alexandria; Heraclius plans the counter-strike that saves Byzantium
Avars and Slavs overrun the Balkan interior to the walls of Thessalonica
In Mecca, Muhammad preaches to a still-pagan Arabia
slices.connectivityNote: The Persian war severs the Egyptian grain fleets and the eastern land routes; Avar wars close the Balkans.

entities.name: Byzantine Empire
entities.note: Persians camp on the Bosphorus shore; Avars in the Balkans. Heraclius nearly moved the capital to Carthage.

entities.name: Sassanid Persia
entities.note: Khusrau II holds Syria, Egypt and the East — the last and greatest Persian overreach.

entities.name: Avar Khaganate
entities.note: The khagan takes Byzantine tribute and drives Slav columns to the Aegean.

entities.name: Brythonic kingdoms
entities.note: Strathclyde, Wales and Brittany — the unconquered Roman-British west.

entities.name: Gaelic Irish kingdoms
entities.note: Uí Néill, Munster and Connacht kings; monasteries are Europe's lamp this century.

entities.name: Pictland
entities.note: Kings of Fortriu beyond the Forth.

entities.name: Arab tribes of the Hejaz fringe

relations.note: The last great war of antiquity — Persia holds the whole Byzantine east
Avar-Slav pressure on Thessalonica and Thrace; joint siege of Constantinople comes in 626
Grinding contest for the Italian interior
Northumbria under Edwin drives into the Brythonic north
Suinthila is expelling the last imperial garrisons of Spania
Frontier skirmishes along the Enns

slices.label: The Arab conquests
events: Arab armies rule Syria, Egypt and Mesopotamia; the last Sassanid shah flees east (murdered 651)
First Arab fleet sacks Cyprus (649) — the Mediterranean balance tips
Slavs are now settled through the Balkan interior to the Peloponnese
slices.connectivityNote: Conquest chaos: the Levant changes masters, but a single caliphal market is quietly forming from Egypt to Iran.

entities.name: Byzantine Empire
entities.note: The empire has lost Syria, Egypt and Africa's hinterland in a generation; Anatolia is the fortress.

entities.name: Slavic tribes
entities.note: From the Elbe to the Aegean interior — Samo's rebel realm (623-58) defies the Avars.

entities.name: Rashidun Caliphate
entities.note: From Medina, the caliphs rule Syria (636), Egypt (641) and a collapsing Persia.

entities.name: Visigothic Kingdom
entities.note: Reccared's Catholic kingdom rules all Iberia; Byzantine Spania expelled by 624.

entities.name: Old Great Bulgaria (Kubrat)
entities.note: Kubrat's Great Bulgaria between Don and Kuban — Khazar hammer about to fall.

relations.note: Syria, Egypt and Armenia lost; Arab fleets now raid Cyprus
Raids probe past Tripoli toward Ifriqiya (Sufetula 647)
Sclaveniae hold the Balkan interior; Constans II campaigns against them (658)
Kubrat, baptized in Constantinople, allies against the Avars
Alpine passes quiet between the two kingdoms

slices.label: Bulgars on the Danube
events: Greek fire breaks the four-year Arab siege of Constantinople (678)
Asparukh's Bulgars cross the Danube — the First Bulgarian Empire is born (681)
Khazar khaganate now rules the steppe from the Don to the Caspian
slices.connectivityNote: Arab-Byzantine naval war makes the eastern Mediterranean a battle zone; the west trades in local coasting runs.

entities.name: Umayyad Caliphate
entities.note: Muawiya's dynasty rules from Damascus; the 674-678 siege of Constantinople just failed.

entities.name: Bulgar Khanate of Asparukh
entities.note: Asparukh's horde crosses the Danube this year; Byzantium recognizes the khanate in 681.

entities.name: Khazar Khaganate
entities.note: Heirs of the western Turks; they crushed Great Bulgaria and take tribute from the steppe.

relations.note: The 674-678 siege failed; Muawiya pays tribute for a truce
Constantine IV's army routed at Ongal; the Bulgars take Moesia
First Arab-Khazar war contests the Caucasus passes
Pippin of Herstal pushes toward the Rhine mouth
Duchies of Spoleto and Benevento gnaw at imperial Italy

slices.label: Spain falls in a summer
events: Tariq crosses at Gibraltar; King Roderic falls at Guadalete — Visigothic Spain collapses in months
Justinian II slain — Byzantium burns through six emperors in twenty years
Umayyad North Africa complete: Carthage fell 698, Tangier 708
slices.connectivityNote: Within the vast Umayyad realm goods flow from the Indus to Tangier, but the Mediterranean divide deepens.

entities.name: Umayyad Caliphate
entities.note: Tariq's Berber army lands at Gibraltar in April — Iberia's conquest has begun.

entities.name: Visigothic Kingdom
entities.note: Roderic dead at Guadalete; Toledo falling; the kingdom dissolves within five years.

entities.name: Frisian Kingdom
entities.note: Radbod's pagan kingdom controls the Rhine-mouth trade at Dorestad.

entities.name: Cyprus condominium
entities.note: Since 688 Byzantium and the caliphate split Cyprus's taxes — a unique shared island.

relations.note: Guadalete: Tariq's 12,000 destroy the kingdom in one battle
Annual raids into Anatolia; the great siege of 717 is coming
Contest for Derbent and the Caucasus
Tervel, made Caesar, propped Justinian II back on his throne (705)
Radbod fights the Carolingian mayors for the Rhine delta

slices.label: The Umayyad high-water mark
events: Charles Martel breaks the Arab raiding army between Tours and Poitiers
Leo III, victor of the 717 siege, decrees iconoclasm (730)
Pelayo's Asturias clings on in the Cantabrian mountains (Covadonga 722)
slices.connectivityNote: Umayyad unity at maximum: dirhams and ideas circulate caliphate-wide; Francia and Italy live off local exchange.

entities.name: Umayyad Caliphate
entities.note: From the Indus to the Atlantic — the largest empire the world had yet seen.

entities.name: Frankish Kingdom (Charles Martel)
entities.note: Charles Martel, mayor of the palace, breaks the Arab raiders between Tours and Poitiers.

entities.name: Kingdom of Asturias
entities.note: Pelayo's mountain rump after Covadonga (722) — the seed of the Reconquista.

relations.note: Tours-Poitiers: Charles Martel halts the raid from al-Andalus
Leo III and the Anatolian themes absorb yearly razzias
Second Arab-Khazar war rages; Marwan's great raid comes in 737
Mountain skirmishes after Covadonga (722)
Treaty of 716 fixes tribute and border markets

slices.label: The Abbasid revolution
events: Abbasid revolution: the Umayyads annihilated at the Zab; the caliphate refounded from Iraq
Lombard king Aistulf closes on Byzantine Ravenna — the exarchate falls in 751
The Mediterranean is a war frontier: gold coin and papyrus vanish north of the Alps
slices.connectivityNote: Pirenne's nadir: the sea is a frontier, papyrus and gold vanish north of the Alps; Frisian and Adriatic traders persist.

entities.name: Abbasid Caliphate
entities.note: Revolution from Khurasan: the caliphate refounded, soon ruled from Baghdad (762).

entities.name: al-Andalus under Fihrid governors
entities.note: The dynasty is slaughtered in the east; Iberia drifts under al-Fihri until an Umayyad refugee arrives (756).

entities.name: Lombard Kingdom
entities.note: Aistulf presses the exarchate — Ravenna falls to him in 751.

entities.name: Berber tribes
entities.note: The Great Berber Revolt (740-43) tore the Maghreb from the caliphate.

entities.name: Barghawata Confederacy
entities.note: Kharijite-inspired Berber confederacy of the Atlantic plain with its own prophet and Koran.

relations.note: The revolution devours the old dynasty; one prince flees west
Aistulf strangles Ravenna — the exarchate dies in 751
Border raids across the Weser presage the Saxon wars
Constantine V readies nine campaigns against Pliska
Frontier raiding resumes as the new caliphate settles in

slices.label: Charlemagne takes the Iron Crown
events: Charlemagne takes Pavia and the Iron Crown — the Lombard kingdom annexed
Abd al-Rahman I, the Umayyad who got away, rules al-Andalus from Córdoba (756)
The Donation of Pepin (756) has made the pope a territorial prince
slices.connectivityNote: Carolingian order helps overland routes; Radhanite Jewish merchants begin linking Francia to the caliphate.

entities.name: Carolingian Frankish Kingdom
entities.note: Charlemagne takes Pavia this year; the Lombard crown passes to the Franks.

entities.name: Emirate of Córdoba (al-Andalus)
entities.note: Abd al-Rahman I, last Umayyad, built an independent emirate at Córdoba in 756.

entities.name: Avar Khaganate
entities.note: Ring-bound and quarrelsome — Charlemagne destroys the khaganate in 795-96.

entities.name: Papal States
entities.note: Carved from the exarchate by Pepin's Donation (756); confirmed by Charlemagne.

entities.name: Principality of Benevento
entities.note: Benevento escapes Charlemagne — Lombard princes rule the southern interior for centuries.

relations.note: Pavia annexed this year; Benevento alone keeps the Lombard cause alive
Patrician of the Romans — the Frankish-papal axis
The thirty-year Saxon wars have begun (772)
Abbasid landing crushed by Abd al-Rahman I (763)
Raid and counter-raid across the empty Duero
Constantine V's Danube offensives grind on

slices.label: An emperor in the West again
events: Charlemagne crowned Roman Emperor in St Peter's on Christmas Day
Harun al-Rashid's Baghdad is the richest city on earth; his elephant walks to Aachen
The Avar khaganate is gone (796) — its treasure hoard carted to Francia
slices.connectivityNote: Two superpowers at peace internally: Abbasid golden-age trade and Carolingian roads; Baltic emporia (Dorestad, Hedeby) rise.

entities.name: Carolingian Empire
entities.note: Crowned emperor on Christmas Day 800 — Saxony, Italy, the Spanish March, tributary Slavs.

entities.name: Aghlabid Emirate
entities.note: Ibrahim ibn al-Aghlab made hereditary emir of Ifriqiya this year for 40,000 dinars a year.

entities.name: Serbian Principality
entities.note: Vlastimirović princes consolidate the Serb tribes between Byzantium and the Bulgars.

entities.name: Rustamid Imamate
entities.note: Ibadi imamate at Tahert — a Kharijite merchant republic on the Saharan trade.

entities.name: Idrisid Emirate
entities.note: Idris, an Alid refugee, founded a Shi'a-tinged realm at Fez (788).

relations.note: Charlemagne and Harun al-Rashid exchange embassies — and an elephant
Frankish siege of Barcelona under way — the city falls in 801
Frosty peace: two emperors, one title problem
Irene buys truces; Harun's raids reach Ancyra
Bulgars and Franks divide the corpse of the Avar khaganate
Alfonso II sacks Lisbon (798) and courts Aachen

slices.label: Verdun: Francia divided
events: Treaty of Verdun splits the Carolingian empire into West, Middle and East Francia
Viking fleets winter in the rivers: Dublin founded 841, Nantes sacked 843
Aghlabid armies grind through Byzantine Sicily (Palermo 831); Kenneth MacAlpin unites Picts and Scots
slices.connectivityNote: Viking raids scourge the coasts yet open river arteries; Arab silver dirhams reach the Baltic in bulk.

entities.name: West Francia
entities.note: Charles the Bald's share at Verdun; Vikings winter at the river mouths.

entities.name: Middle Francia
entities.note: Lothair keeps the imperial title, Aachen and Italy — a corridor realm doomed to partition.

entities.name: East Francia
entities.note: Louis the German's Frankish, Saxon and Bavarian lands east of the Rhine.

entities.name: Aghlabid Emirate
entities.note: Palermo taken 831; the grinding conquest of Byzantine Sicily is half done.

entities.name: Irish kingdoms
entities.note: Uí Néill high-kings contest with Norse longphorts — Dublin founded 841.

entities.name: Great Moravia
entities.note: Mojmir's Slavic state above the Danube; Rastislav will invite Cyril and Methodius (863).

entities.name: Magyars (Levedia)
entities.note: Seven tribes on the Pontic steppe, paying loose tribute to the Khazars.

entities.name: Kingdom of Alba
entities.note: Kenneth MacAlpin unites Picts and Scots this very year.

entities.name: Kingdom of Pamplona
entities.note: Basque kingdom of Pamplona (824), wedged between Franks and Córdoba.

entities.name: Emirate of Crete
entities.note: Andalusi exiles seized Crete (824); Chandax is the Aegean's corsair nest.

entities.name: Georgian Bagratid principalities & Abkhazia
entities.note: Bagratid Tao-Klarjeti and the kings of Abkhazia divide the Georgian lands.

relations.note: Verdun: three brothers partition Charlemagne's empire in peace
Louis the German deposes Mojmir (846)
Viking fleets sack Nantes and Rouen; Paris pays in 845
Messina falls (842-43); Sicily bleeds
Amorium sacked 838; the frontier war is annual
Ramiro I fights off raids by land and Vikings by sea
Presian's invasion broken by Vlastimir's Serbs

slices.label: Vikings, Meerssen and the Danelaw
events: Meerssen: East and West Francia carve up Lotharingia between them
The Great Heathen Army has felled Northumbria and East Anglia — the Danelaw takes shape
Malta falls to the Aghlabids; Constantinople and Rome contest the new Bulgarian church
slices.connectivityNote: The Varangian river roads hum — Volga and Dnieper silver, furs and slaves; the western sea remains raider-infested.

entities.name: Kingdom of Italy (Emperor Louis II)
entities.note: Emperor Louis II rules Italy alone; Lotharingia carved up at Meerssen this year.

entities.name: First Bulgarian Empire
entities.note: Boris accepted baptism from Constantinople (864); a Slavic church is forming.

entities.name: Great Moravia
entities.note: Rastislav betrayed and blinded this year; Svatopluk will push the realm to its peak.

entities.name: Wessex & English Mercia
entities.note: Æthelred and young Alfred stand alone against the Danes.

entities.name: The Danelaw
entities.note: The Great Heathen Army holds York (866) and East Anglia (869); Wessex is next.

entities.name: Welsh principalities
entities.note: Rhodri Mawr of Gwynedd unites most of Wales against Danes and Mercians.

entities.name: Kingdom of Brittany
entities.note: Salomon styles himself king; Brittany won its autonomy at Ballon (845).

entities.name: Rus of Novgorod (Rurikid)
entities.note: Rurik's Norse-Slav polity at Novgorod (862) taps the river roads to the silver of the East.

entities.name: Duchy of Croatia
entities.note: Trpimir's duchy (845) between Frankish and Byzantine overlords.

relations.note: East Anglia destroyed (869); the Danes turn on Wessex
Rastislav captured and blinded; Svatopluk seizes power
Malta lost (870); Louis II and Basil I retake Bari (871)
Council of 869-70 grants Bulgaria its archbishopric
After the 860 raid, furs and slaves flow south for silk
Rivals sharing the Volga-Dnieper silver routes
Salomon extracts land and royal rank from Charles the Bald

slices.label: Magyars on the plain
events: Magyars seize the Pannonian plain (895-900); Great Moravia will be gone by 906
Alfred the Great is dead (899); Wessex and the Danelaw brace for the reconquest
Oleg's Rus rules the river road from Novgorod through Kyiv (882)
slices.connectivityNote: Radhanites and Varangians carry dirhams and silk around a fractured west; Umayyad Córdoba and Byzantium re-anchor the sea.

entities.name: Byzantine Empire
entities.note: Leo VI's themes hold firm; the navy plans the reconquest of Crete.

entities.name: East Francia
entities.note: Louis the Child, aged six; Magyar raids begin in earnest.

entities.name: Emirate of Córdoba (al-Andalus)
entities.note: Ibn Hafsun's decades-long revolt hollows the emirate from the southern mountains.

entities.name: Tulunid Egypt & Syria
entities.note: Ibn Tulun's heirs rule Egypt and Syria; Abbasid armies reclaim it in 905.

entities.name: Kingdom of Italy
entities.note: Berengar and rivals contest the crown; Magyars raid the Po plain (899).

entities.name: Kievan Rus
entities.note: Oleg took Kyiv (882) and united the Dnieper route from Novgorod to the steppe edge.

entities.name: Pechenegs
entities.note: New masters of the Pontic steppe, having driven the Magyars west.

entities.name: Abbasid Caliphate
entities.note: The caliphate keeps Iraq and the Jazira but the provinces slip away one by one.

entities.name: First Bulgarian Empire (Simeon)
entities.note: Simeon, Byzantine-educated, beat the empire at Bulgarophygon (896); he dreams of Constantinople.

entities.name: Kingdom of the Anglo-Saxons
entities.note: Edward the Elder succeeds Alfred (899); the reconquest of the Danelaw is planned.

entities.name: The Danelaw
entities.note: Danish kings at York and East Anglia; Alfred's burhs cage them from the south.

entities.name: Kingdoms of Burgundy (Upper & Lower)
entities.note: Rudolph I (888) in the Jura, Louis the Blind in Provence.

entities.name: Magyar tribal confederation
entities.note: Árpád's tribes seized Pannonia 895-900, driven west by the Pechenegs.

entities.name: Bagratid Armenia
entities.note: Ashot I crowned by the caliph (884) — Armenia's first king in nearly five centuries.

entities.name: Sardinian giudicati
entities.note: Byzantine ties lapsed; four native judges (giudicati) rule the island.

entities.name: Khazar Khaganate
entities.note: Still astride the Volga trade, but Rus and Pechenegs erode the western khaganate.

entities.name: Great Moravia (rump)
entities.note: Mojmir II's rump fights Magyars and Franks; the state vanishes by 906.

entities.name: Cyprus condominium
entities.note: Still jointly taxed by Byzantium and the caliphate after two centuries.

relations.note: Pannonia seized; Italy raided (899); Bavaria is next
The horsemen dismember Svatopluk's inheritance
Uneasy truce after Simeon's victory at Bulgarophygon (896)
Caliphal armies prepare to reclaim Egypt (done 905)
The Dnieper route booms; Oleg's treaty raid comes in 907
Æthelwold's revolt sputters; Edward eyes the Five Boroughs
Alfonso III pushes the frontier to the Duero
The Pechenegs hold the steppe they drove the Magyars from

uncertainties: Verification pass was knowledge-based: the coordinator disabled web searching mid-task, so sources list the reference works underlying the draft rather than live queries.
620: Persian-held CIL/EGY/SYR/LEV shown as Sassanid though administration was a brief occupation regime; Anatolia kept Byzantine despite deep raids.
711 is mid-conquest in Iberia: only AND+CAS_S given to the Umayyads (Guadalete July, Toledo late 711); the Visigothic rump keeps the rest until 712-16.
Balearics (BAL) kept nominally Byzantine/autonomous 620-870 despite Arab raids; assigned to al-Andalus at 900 slightly ahead of the 902-903 conquest.
Cyprus shown as the 688 Byzantine-Arab tax condominium 711-900; era08 shows it simply Byzantine at 930 — join note.
NAP (Campania-Apulia) given to Lombards/Benevento from 650 although coastal Naples, Amalfi and Gaeta stayed nominally Byzantine throughout.
BOH cell fused Bohemia+Moravia: assigned to Great Moravia 843-870 (Bohemia was only loosely tributary), to Přemyslid Bohemia at 900.
SUI cell straddles Alemannia and Burgundy: east_francia at 870, burgundy_kingdom at 900 to match era08's 930 slice.
Barghawata kept in MAR 750-900 (they held the Atlantic plain to the 11th c.); era08 folds MAR into the Idrisids at 930 — flagged as contested on the Idrisid side instead.
Sicily assigned to the Aghlabids from 843 (Palermo 831) though Syracuse held to 878 and Taormina to 902 — marked contested both sides.
Croatia founded 845 (Trpimir) rather than the canonical 925 kingdom date; Burgundy founded 888 rather than canonical 933 — both to join era08's usage.
kievan_rus founded 862 in the 870 slice (Rurik at Novgorod) but 882 at 900 (canonical, Oleg's union) — deliberate re-founding echo.
Magyars at 843 placed in Levedia (STE+MDA cells); their exact 9th-century range on the Pontic steppe is scholarly guesswork.
Venice, Amalfi and the Dalmatian city communes are too small for their cells and are noted in text only; Volga Bulgars lie off-map.
Slav tribute zones (UKR/BLR paying Khazars, Sorbian marches) simplified to slavs_early; Danelaw boundary at 900 simplified to ENG_E+ENG_N with English Mercia holding ENG_M.
Population figures interpolate McEvedy & Jones; the 650-700 European trough (~25-26M map-wide) and slow 9th-century recovery are encoded in per-entity numbers.
